entries.brief: ONE COMPACT PORTABLE VETERINARY MEDICINE KIT for military horses, early nineteenth-century conceptual equipment. A small open dark-brown wooden fitted chest with modest brass hinges contains three simple cork-stoppered amber-glass medicine bottles, a neatly rolled nearly-white linen bandage and a plain small steel instrument, all resting in coherent internal compartments. The hinged lid is open, plain and unlabelled. ONE large worn dark-iron HORSESHOE leans upright against the near side of the chest, prominently readable and attached visually to this single group, signifying equine care. Keep the kit dominant, the horseshoe clearly subordinate but identifiable, readable care supplies rather than a treasure chest. Natural warm wood and off-white cloth, modest glass highlights, no decorative carving or modern bag. NO blood, injury, exposed organs, red cross, medical symbols, labels, papers, scattered medicine, shiny crystals or separate background horse. This is an interpretation of regimental veterinary care, not an exact named military kit.

entries.brief: ONE eighteenth-century brass ALTAZIMUTH THEODOLITE on a short natural-oak THREE-LEGGED TRIPOD, symbolizing a trained military engineer's precise field surveying. The dominant upper apparatus consists of a broad horizontal brass graduated circular plate with a small central covered compass, one visibly attached vertical semicircular brass angle arc, and ONE straight narrow brass sighting telescope crossing the top at a slight upward tilt. The single telescope is firmly mounted on a functional pivot bracket linked to the vertical arc; no floating or intersecting tubes. The entire instrument sits on one central metal mounting stem securely joined to the tripod's wooden head. Exactly three coherent wooden tripod legs, naturally splayed, with all three complete feet visible and within the canvas. Short sturdy tripod, generous scale for the telescope and angle arcs so they stay readable at icon size. Warm muted brass with patina, darker metal fittings, brown oak legs, modest glass lenses. The circle and arc use simple fine engraved unlabeled ticks only: no letters, numbers or readable markings. Slightly elevated three-quarter view, entire connected silhouette, no huge pedestal or floor shadow. The eighteenth-century collection images guide the instrument concept, not an exact replicated specimen. No map, paper, drawing board, alidade table, basket, gabion, shovel, soldier, castle, flag, cable, modern laser, digital screen, green plastic or camera.

entries.brief: A COMPACT EARLY NINETEENTH-CENTURY HORSE-ARTILLERY TRANSPORT GROUP, in elevated three-quarter view along a diagonal so the silhouette fills a square. Exactly TWO healthy chestnut/bay horses stand side by side at the front in plain period brown-leather draught harness, with anatomically coherent four legs each, natural hooves, heads, tails and no rider. They are connected by taut coherent traces to ONE small wooden two-wheeled artillery LIMBER carrying a modest plain closed ammunition chest. The limber is attached by a visible functional pintle hitch to the tail end of ONE lightweight muzzle-loading FIELD CANNON carriage behind it. The cannon has its own ONE axle and TWO large wooden spoked iron-rimmed wheels, a connected wooden trail, and ONE continuous straight restrained bronze barrel held on trunnions; the barrel points away from the horses, backward along the same travel axis. FOUR vehicle wheels total: two limber wheels and two gun wheels, coherent axles rather than floating extra wheels. Use weathered warm wood, muted bronze, dark iron and warm brown horses. Clearly distinguish the horse team, limber and light gun as one connected apparatus. For icon-scale this is a deliberately reduced symbolic pair, NOT a claim that two horses were a full standard gun team. NO soldiers, battlefield, soil, road, grass base, flags, plume, uniforms, ornate carving, modern recoil system, gun shield, rubber tire, red cross, logos or writing. No disconnected cannon, loose horse heads, bent tube or pointy ornamental wheel hubs.
